answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock $100 for 30 days to receive a fixed daily trading quota. Splitting into 1,000 identities then ties up $100,000 without increasing trades per dollar of collateral. The public ledger is a lantern for auditors: they can verify each bond before letting an agent bridge into the market. A ripple of new identities therefore carries a proportional capital cost, even when account creation is free.
